title: CapCut guide: sales videos for small businesses
description: How to use free CapCut to make 30-second sales videos for TikTok and Reels: filming, editing, automatic captions, music you can legally use and privacy.
author: Cross Tech Edu
cover_alt: A shop owner editing a sales video in CapCut on a laptop, with a phone on a stand showing automatic captions
body:
**CapCut** is a free video editor that turns clips filmed on your phone into **short sales videos** for TikTok, Facebook Reels and YouTube Shorts: add text, music and captions, and cut out the boring bits. You don't need a fancy camera or editing skills; a phone and 30 minutes are enough for your first video.

This CapCut guide walks through it step by step: preparing to film, editing a 30-second video, automatic captions, choosing music you are allowed to use, what is free and what is paid, and privacy.

## 1. What can free CapCut still do?

CapCut is made by ByteDance, TikTok's parent company. Since 2025 CapCut has moved quite a few features behind its paid plans, but **basic editing is still free**:

- Cutting, joining and reordering video clips and photos.
- Adding text, music, transitions and colour filters.
- **Automatic captions**, with a limited allowance on the free plan.
- Exporting in **1080p**, which looks sharp on social media.

Templates, effects and AI tools marked **Pro** either require payment or add a watermark to the export. If you stick to free features, your video exports **without a watermark**.

## 2. Before you film

A good sales video doesn't need to be elaborate, but it does need a few basics:

- **Film vertically** (hold the phone upright): TikTok, Reels and Shorts are all vertical.
- **Use good light:** film near a window during the day and avoid shooting into the light.
- **Shoot several 3–5 second clips** instead of one long take: product close-ups, packing an order, a customer using it, the shop itself.
- **Wipe the camera lens** first. It sounds obvious, but it is the most common reason for blurry videos.

> **Tip:** a cheap phone stand keeps the picture steady and looks far more professional than filming by hand.

## 3. Editing a 30-second sales video, step by step

Install **CapCut** from Google Play or the App Store and check the developer is **Bytedance**. You can sign in with TikTok, Google or Facebook.

### Step 1: Create a project and add your clips

Tap **New project**, select your clips and photos **in the order you want them**, then add them. CapCut lines them up on the **timeline**, the long strip at the bottom of the screen.

### Step 2: Trim the extra bits

Tap a clip on the timeline and drag its left and right edges to cut the start and end. To cut a clip in two, move the white line to the spot and tap **Split**. Aim for **15–30 seconds** in total.

### Step 3: Add text

Tap **Text** → **Add text** and type your main message for the first 3 seconds, for example *"Homemade bread, out of the oven at 6 a.m."*. Keep text in the middle of the screen; TikTok's buttons cover the bottom edge.

### Step 4: Add music

Tap **Audio** to pick music. Turn the music down if you are speaking in the video. Read section 5 on copyright before you choose a track.

### Step 5: Export

Tap **Export** in the top corner and choose **1080p**. The video is saved to your phone's gallery, ready to post on TikTok, Facebook or Zalo (Vietnam's most popular messaging app).

## 4. Automatic captions

Most people scroll **with the sound off**, so captions help them follow what you say.

1. Tap **Text** → **Auto captions**.
2. Choose the spoken language (Vietnamese, English and many others are supported) and start. CapCut listens and types the words for you.
3. **Read every line** and fix mistakes: product names, prices and local words are often misheard.

The free plan limits how much automatic captioning you can do. When you run out, you can still **type captions yourself** with Add text: slower, but completely free.

## 5. Music and copyright in sales videos

This is where many shop owners slip up:

- Not every track in CapCut may be used for **commercial purposes**, and a video promoting your products is commercial.
- **TikTok business accounts** can only use music from TikTok's commercial music library. Using a hit song can get your video muted or removed.
- On Facebook, videos with copyrighted music can also be blocked or muted.

The safest options: choose music marked as **cleared for commercial use**, or **use your own voice** to present the product. A shop owner's real voice often builds more trust than a trending track.

## 6. Templates, and when watermarks appear

CapCut's **template** library lets you pick a template, drop in your clips and get a video cut to the beat. It's quick, but:

- Templates marked **Pro** add a watermark or ask you to pay when exporting.
- Many templates use trending songs that aren't suitable for business accounts (see section 5).
- Template videos look like thousands of others. Editing your own, as in section 3, gives your shop its own style.

> **Note:** if your export has a watermark even though you didn't mean to pay, check the project: there is usually an effect, font or filter marked Pro. Remove it and export again.

## 7. Privacy when using CapCut

CapCut's terms of service, updated in 2025, let it store the content you put into the app on its servers and give the company broad rights to use that content. For a small business this means:

- **Don't put internal information into CapCut:** account books, screens of your sales software, invoices with customer names.
- **Ask permission before filming customers or staff** and using them in videos.
- For important videos (a brand launch, a major campaign), consider a professional video editor or desktop editing software.

## 8. Is CapCut Pro worth it?

Use the free plan for at least a few weeks first. Consider upgrading when:

- You post videos **every day** and keep running out of automatic captions.
- You need AI tools such as video background removal, noise reduction or caption translation.
- You need exports sharper than 1080p.

CapCut has several paid plans and prices vary by region, so check the price shown in the app before paying. **Only buy inside the app**, never a cheap "CapCut Pro account" from a stranger.

## 9. Where to start

1. **Today:** film 5 short clips of your best-selling product and edit them into a 20-second video following section 3.
2. **This week:** make a video where you introduce the product yourself, add automatic captions and fix the typos.
3. **At the weekend:** compare the views of your edited video with your usual photo posts.

Thumbnails and promotional images to go with your videos are quick to make in Canva, see our [Canva guide for small business owners](/en/blog/canva-guide-for-small-business-owners/). To write a script for your video, ask an AI assistant from our list of [free AI tools for small businesses](/en/blog/free-ai-tools-for-small-business/).

*Checked in October 2026. CapCut changes what is free and what is paid fairly often; if you can't find a button as described, look in the app's help section.*
